title: "Module 3 Demo: Final Report"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    embed-resources: true
---

This report is the **final step of the Snakemake pipeline** — and it is yours to
write. Apply what you learned in the dynamic reporting module: read the files
produced by the earlier pipeline steps with code, and turn them into tables,
figures, and inline statistics.

The pipeline has already produced these artifacts for you:

| File | Produced by | Contents |
|------|-------------|----------|
| `work/1_derived.csv` | `1_derive.py` (Python) | columns `year`, `value`, `value_centered` |
| `work/2_summary.txt` | `2_summary.R` (R) | `key=value` summary lines |
| `work/3_processed.csv` | `3_polars_process.py` (polars) | adds a `value_centered_z` column |

Work in whichever language you followed in Module 2 — R and Python are both
available in the workshop container. After each change, re-run the pipeline and
open `results/4_report.html`:

```bash
snakemake --cores 1
```

Notice that only the `final_report` rule re-runs. Snakemake sees that nothing
upstream of this file changed.

## Setup

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
**Your task**

Add a code chunk that loads the libraries you need.
:::

## Derived data

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
**Your task**

Read `work/1_derived.csv` in a code chunk and display it as a table with a
caption.
:::

## Summary statistics

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
**Your task**

Read `work/2_summary.txt` in a code chunk and print its lines. Reading it with code keeps the report
*dynamic*: whenever the pipeline re-runs, the report picks up the new numbers
automatically. A static alternative would be the
`{{{< include work/2_summary.txt >}}}` shortcode. The Nextflow variant of this
demo does exactly that. But then nothing is computed at render time.
:::

## Processed data

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
**Your task**

Read `work/3_processed.csv` and plot `value_centered_z` over `year`. Give the
chunk a label and a caption with `#| label: fig-zscores` and `#| fig-cap:`,
then refer to the figure in your text with `@fig-zscores`.
:::

## Bonus: inline statistics

::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"}
**Your task**

Report a computed value inside a sentence using inline code, so the number can
never go stale. For example:

``` markdown
The processed dataset contains `{{r}} nrow(processed)` rows.
```

``` markdown
The processed dataset contains `{{python}} len(processed)` rows.
```
:::
